title.en: Shanghai: The Vertical Surge of Pudong

subtitle: How a curve in the Huangpu River rose into the sky
intro: This is Shanghai today where the Huangpu curves past the Bund into Pudong. Let us take every building away, and watch it rise from mudflats into the sky.
outro: In thirty years, Pudong transformed from farmland into the world's most dramatic vertical skyline.
credits: Historical dates: Shanghai Municipal Archives & CTBUH
Directed by MiniMax M3.1 Flash via SandBase

eras.label: The Treaty Port · 1843–1910
eras.narration: Along the western mudflats of the Huangpu, international merchants laid the first stone quays of the Bund.

eras.label: Stone Along the Bund · 1911–1937
eras.narration: Granite banks, the Customs clock tower, and the art-deco crown of the Peace Hotel transformed Shanghai into Paris of the East.

eras.label: Farmland Across the River · 1938–1989
eras.narration: For fifty years, while the western shore hummed with density, the eastern peninsula of Pudong remained quiet farmland, warehouses, and shipyards.

eras.label: The Great Awakening · 1990–1994
eras.narration: In nineteen ninety, China designated Pudong a Special Economic Zone. Four years later, the Oriental Pearl Tower sparked a vertical renaissance.

eras.label: Pagoda in Steel · 1995–2000
eras.narration: Rising eighty-eight storeys, Jin Mao Tower joined traditional Chinese pagoda symmetry with eighty-eight floors of steel and glass.

eras.label: The Supertall Trinity · 2001–2015
eras.narration: The World Financial Center carved a portal into the clouds, before the spiraling dragon form of Shanghai Tower topped out at six hundred thirty-two metres.

eras.label: The Vertical Horizon · 2016–2026
eras.narration: Across two centuries of water and ambition, Shanghai built the highest density of human ingenuity on earth.
